main_body: A tree-stump chopping block (round body) with an axe blade stuck in the top; the stump is the main volume.
top_band: Lighter orange-brown (#b77246) ellipse top at rows 4-7 in the middle column, under the grey axe blade at rows 1-3. A short step to the darker bark face (#9a5435) follows at row 8.
evidence: The top reads as a rounded ellipse 4 rows tall, wider than the axe, with its corners cut in. Below it a distinctly darker bark face of about 6 rows carries a dark bark line and a shadowed right side. At x=11 the step is 126 to 68 L. At the centre column the step is only 23 L, but it is a clear hue and tone change and the rounded top silhouette reads as a surface from above. There is no distinct front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the evidence is moderate rather than strong. It still reads as a 3/4 round body like the guide's barrel with an ellipse top, not a flat band or rim.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours against 38-40 in both references, and a median of 10 colours per tile against 17-20. Its wood ramp has about 4 steps (b77246, 9a5435, 6d3b15, 63310b, 411e05) where Beodeul uses 5-6. There are no flat 5x5 fills, which is good, but the grain is limited to a couple of dark bark marks. 53% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is partly near-black rather than a consistent dark wood tone. Next to the stall and well it looks thinner and simpler, with less surface texture and less colour variation in the ramp.
